$comment: The one declared registry of every spec-repo conformance check (rfc-decision-19997e24, issue #495). validate-all.mjs is a loop over this file's `always`-tier entries, in array order — order matters for at least one entry (see `afterId`), so this stays a JSON array, never re-sorted. `check-checks-registry-membership.mjs` (itself listed below) fails the build if a `scripts/check-*.mjs` file on disk is missing from this file. Fields per entry: `id` (stable, kebab-case), `script` (path passed to `runScript`, relative to scripts/ exactly as today — no renames), `args` (argv passed to the script), `tier` (`always` run by `node scripts/validate-all.mjs`; `pinned-cli` needs the pinned `srs` binary from scripts/fetch-pinned-srs.mjs and is not runnable from plain `node`; `ci-only` is reached only by a CI workflow step with no local entry point), `cell` (the Pattern Grid slug this check guards against drift in, per scripts/lib/pattern-grid-cells.json), `governing` (the RFC/decision/issue that introduced the rule), `description` (what the check actually asserts and why), and optionally `afterId` (this check must run after the named id — an execution-order dependency, not just a display grouping) and `expiry` (an issue tracking when a grandfathered check is expected to retire). This is a stepping stone toward checks-as-records (rfc-decision-19997e24's trajectory clause, handed to the #490 fold) — the JSON here is meant to become a generated projection, not a permanent hand-authored artifact.

checks.description: Every package discovered under srs/package/** and packages/** (see discoverPackages() below) validates its fields/types/views/documentViews/themes/relationTypes/vocabularies/lifecycles/blueprints/protocols against their declared schemas. Runs once per discovered package — args are supplied per-invocation, not read from this entry.
No two packages, and no two definitions listed within a resolved package's index, may claim one UUID. A UUID is the primary identity in SRS and must be globally stable.
Every instance file under records/ validates against its declared structural schema, and every relation resolves an installed relationType (#465: fails the run, not just prints, when one does not).

Boundary rules keeping RFC proposal material separate from active spec state: a proposal-artifact-path must never point at active package/ or docs/schema/ state, rfc-targets-section relations resolve on both ends, and the RFC-004 proposed-package validates against its own proposed schemas without touching live ones.

Every accepted/implemented RFC declares a non-empty srs-integration manifest whose tokens all resolve, its .md Status line matches the record's rfc-status, and (for RFCs created 2026-08-23 or later, individually-grandfathered ones excepted) its .md carries a complete, self-consistent `## Charter alignment` section.
The RFC-032 field-type model's owner acceptance condition made runnable: every hard meta-model shape is expressible as a fieldType, and every fieldType projects to well-formed JSON Schema 2020-12.
migrate-rfc-032-field-type.mjs transforms its fixtures correctly (valueType -> fieldType).

Regenerates the 24 RFC-032 Testability fixture Field files from its in-script table and proves them conformant. Other checks (e.g. field-name-convention) read this run's output, so anything reading tests/ fixtures must run after this entry.
The valueType -> fieldType migration stays fully applied: no field anywhere may still carry the legacy scalar valueType.

No Type may assign a Field as repeatable via the deprecated repeatable/minItems/maxItems trio unless that Field's own fieldType independently declares cardinality: list — Field.fieldType.cardinality is the sole cardinality mechanism.
The vocabularyRef migration stays fully applied: no Field definition under tests/rfc-032/package/fields may still carry a legacy "namespace/name@version" vocabularyRef pattern string.

checks.governing: RFC-023 Change A/B; srs#480; RFC-040 Change I
checks.description: No sourceRef under srs/records may still carry the legacy relationType field; names the migration explicitly rather than surfacing only as a generic schema-validation error.
The substrate escape-bag rename stays fully applied: no Term, RelationTypeDefinition, LifecycleState, or LifecycleTransition anywhere in the repo may still carry the legacy `properties` key.

Field.name is snake_case everywhere a Field definition is found, across every carrier shape (plain JSON, .srsj/.srspkg bundles, the legacy valueType carrier). Must run after the RFC-032 conformance fixture regenerates its Field files, or it reads the previous run's output.

Every definition kind docs/schema/2.0/package-manifest.json declares (fields, types, views, ...) resolves to an actual schema file in docs/schema/2.0/ — a declared kind is not real unless it reaches its schema.
package-bundle.json's $defs.Reference.definitionType enum is GENERATED from package-manifest.json's declared definition kinds, so the two lists cannot independently diverge (finding A6).
view.json's RecordPropertyView.property enum is GENERATED from record.json's declared top-level properties after RFC-041's explicit exclusions, so the two lists cannot independently diverge.

Every discovered, loading record is reachable from a declared presentation (a contains edge from a query root, root-container membership, or the RFC-016 invariants projection) or its invisibility is declared in scripts/publication-reachability-exclusions.json with a live reason and issue.
Every com.semanticops.spec/invariant record lives directly under records/invariants/, the RFC-016 projection root — with no exclusion-list escape, unlike the #285 reachability guard.

docs/charter/decision-compass.md stays bidirectionally in sync with the charter-class decision records it surfaces: every roster id resolves to a real record and is cited somewhere in the body, and every body citation resolves to a real record.
Every com.semanticops.spec/rfc-decision record dated 2026-08-23 or later carries at least one cell:<slug> tag naming a slug from the Pattern Grid vocabulary.

checks.governing: srs#308; srs#311; srs#391 (and every guard added since)
checks.description: Every enforcement check demonstrably fails on the violation it exists to catch, and passes without it — asserted on the failure message, not just the exit code, so a guard that has never been watched fail cannot pass for the wrong reason.

Every scripts/check-*.mjs file on disk is declared as a `script` value somewhere in this registry — piecemeal addition of a new check without registering it fails the build. Self-referential: this very script is itself declared here.
The frozen-seed self-hosted metamodel package (srs/package/metamodel/**) stays in sync with its generator (scripts/gen-metamodel-package.mjs) — a regenerate produces an empty diff.
Per-field bootstrap-closure demonstration: every fieldType in the metamodel package projects, via the projectField stand-in, to its frozen-seed authoritative fragment.
The RFC-035 JSON Schema emitter's whole-entity output is byte-for-byte reproducible against its committed goldens.
The RFC-035 emitter's whole-entity output is a subset of the frozen seed over the covered authoritative features (discharges RFC-033 [R4](b)).
A full regenerate of docs/schema/2.0/{field,type}.json from the metamodel package equals the committed files, modulo only the documented-divergence register in projection-rules.md.

Golden fixtures for effective-Type resolution on domain (non-meta-model) Types: standard single-ancestor merge, the definition-facing/instance-facing distinction, and conditional projection (allOf/if/then guards).
Every com.semanticops.spec/generated-type-reference record's content equals a fresh regenerate from its resolved effective Type — the reader-projection generator's own empty-diff gate.
Every ext:discovery scenario carrying an expectedSegments expectation has its segment count and order actually evaluated against conformance/discovery/fixture-repo, not just prose-asserted.

Every docs/schema/2.0/*.json file has a row in docs/schema/2.0/generation-ledger.md (a backticked mention of its filename is sufficient) — the cheap completeness floor srs#522's ledger unit added, so a new schema file cannot land unclassified.

The committed rendered exports under docs/spec/ are byte-identical to a fresh render from the pinned srs CLI release named by SRS_RUST_CLI_TAG. Required CI check and pre-commit hook; invokes validate-all.mjs and `srs repo validate` as its first step, so it is never itself looped inside validate-all.mjs.

The prose pseudo-IDL embedded in spec records and the docs/schema/2.0/*.json JSON Schema files agree on property set, optionality, and declared type, per RFC-031 R1-R3, with known gaps recorded in scripts/idl-schema-conformance-allowlist.json. Wired into check-release-drift.mjs (RFC-031 [R5]), never into validate-all.mjs directly — not in the issue #495 inventory, found during implementation.

The gallery corpus target (docs/spec/examples/gallery-project-v2/) stays a conforming SRS repository: its .srs/ marker resolves as a non-empty directory, and the pinned srs CLI reports zero repo-validate errors against it. Run as its own CI workflow step, not through check-release-drift.mjs or validate-all.mjs — not in the issue #495 inventory, found during implementation.
